messages:
maya: quick recap of the cross-region SSE vs WS run — dropped into the google sheet + images: https://rwd-inf/sheets/bench/pathfinder (charts attached). p50/p95/p99 + steady-state tokens/s measured across A100/H100/L4 in us-west1 / eu-west1 / asia-east1. summary: SSE wins for tail under high concurrency, WS has slightly better p50 at low concurrency. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

simon: can you paste the critical numbers? curious about p99 on H100 with nf4 quant and the kernel used.

maya: sure — quick excerpts: H100 nf4 + flash-attention v2 => p50 85ms, p95 220ms, p99 380ms @ 80 concurrent reqs (streaming/SSE) on us-west1. Non-stream (WS/batched) @ same concurrency: p50 72ms, p95 260ms, p99 490ms. throughput: SSE sustained ~1.9k tokens/s per GPU, WS/batch ~2.4k tokens/s but higher p99.

roland: interesting. so SSE gives more stable tails despite slightly lower peak throughput. any kernel differences between regions?

maya: yes — eu-west1 runs have a slightly older driver combo so Triton fused-attn falls back to generic kernel on some sequence lengths => +30–50ms p95 bump. asia-east1 saw similar. note: L4 int8 behaved oddly at 512 seq, p99 spiked due to kernel fallback.

lia: did you try prefix/KV caching impact? for chat workloads that could change the tradeoff a lot.

maya: quick A/B we did: prefix caching on SSE reduced tokens/s by ~12% but p50 dropped 20–30ms and p99 improved ~15%. For WS/batch, caching made less difference unless you hit large batch sizes (>=8), then both throughput and p99 improved.

perf-bot: automated-run finished: run_id=pf-20260214-03, results uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/pathfinder/pf-20260214-03.json — contains per-kernel breakdown, samples, and generated flamegraphs.

simon: can you drop the curl examples you used to exercise each mode? helps me reproduce.

maya: yep, SSE test (server-sent events) load snippet:```bash
# SSE (long-lived conn, single-stream)
for i in {1..200}; do curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
  "https://api.redwood/v1/stream?model=pathfinder-nf4" &
done
```
WS test (simple parallel conns):```js
// websocket clients: open N sockets and send single request per socket
const ws = new WebSocket(url);
ws.send(JSON.stringify({prompt: '...', max_tokens: 256}));
```

roland: next steps I propose: 1) run L4 kernel sweep with latest driver, 2) add int8 vs nf4 quality check with our eval set (to detect hallucination regressions), 3) run a regional kernel compatibility smoke test and record fallbacks. I'll take 1 & 3.

lia: +1 — I'll own the quality eval (2). please add a short ticket with what inputs to run.

maya: created ticket INF-4298 with links to sheet + perf-bot artifacts. adding a note: for canary deploys, recommend SSE default for chat endpoints in high-concurrency tiers; allow WS for low-concurrency, high-throughput cases. :thumbsup:

simon: awesome, thanks. if we see >20% p99 regressions after quant change, abort rollout and revert to nf4. :thinking_face:

maya: agreed. I'll schedule the follow-up runs for tomorrow morning (us-west window).
